text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- South Korean President Kim Young-sam was given a formal state welcoming ceremony at Hanoi's presidential palace on Wednesday. President Le Duc Anh could not attend because of illness, but sent his greetings.

-- At least 986 people have been killed and many others injured by the almost-unprecedented number of tropical storms and floods which have hit Vietnam so far this year, the Central Committee for Floods and Storm Control said.

-- Visiting South Korea's President Kim Young-sam told Vietnam secretary General Do Muoi that South Korea supports Vietnam's applications to join the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum and the World Trade Organization and will continue development aid programmes for Vietnam.
-- Vietnam has signed the Southeast Asia Nuclear Wepon Free Zone treaty.
-- A $59 million joint venture to build a industrial zone in Hanoi was signed between Japan's Sumitomo Commercial Company and Vietnam's Dong Anh Engineering Company on Wednesday.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong has urged local authorities in the Mekong Delta provinces of Dong Thap and An Giang to find measures to drain floodwaters in the area away to the sea.
